## Refurbished Two-Bedroom First Floor Flat with Private Garden – Tudor Drive, Kingston upon Thames – £1,850 pcm

Situated on the sought-after Tudor Drive in Kingston upon Thames, this recently refurbished first-floor flat offers stylish, comfortable accommodation with the added benefit of a private garden. Available to rent at £1,850 per calendar month, the property is ideally suited to those seeking a well-presented home within easy reach of Kingston town centre, local amenities and transport links.

The flat has been thoughtfully modernised throughout, combining contemporary finishes with a practical layout. The accommodation includes a bright and welcoming reception area, providing a comfortable space for relaxing, dining and entertaining.

There are two bedrooms, comprising a generously sized double bedroom and a versatile single bedroom. The second bedroom could work equally well as a home office, nursery, dressing room or guest room, depending on individual requirements.

The property further benefits from a separate modern fitted kitchen, finished in a clean contemporary style and offering a practical space for everyday cooking. The kitchen is designed with storage and usability in mind, making it a pleasant and functional addition to the home.

A modern luxury bathroom completes the accommodation, featuring high-quality contemporary fittings and a refined finish, creating a calm and stylish space to start or end the day.

One of the property’s standout features is its private garden, offering valuable outdoor space for relaxing, enjoying warmer weather, gardening or al fresco dining. Private outside space is a particularly desirable feature in this well-connected part of Kingston.

Ever popular Tudor Drive, within walking distance of Fern Hill, Latchmere and Kingston Academy schools. Conveniently located for everyday amenities, with local shops, cafés, schools, green spaces and bus routes nearby. Kingston town centre, with its extensive shopping, dining and leisure facilities, is within easy reach, while Kingston railway station provides useful connections towards central London.

Key Features:

- Recently refurbished first-floor flat
- Two bedrooms: one double and one single
- Bright reception/living space
- Modern separate fitted kitchen
- Contemporary luxury bathroom
- Private garden
- Desirable Tudor Drive location
- Convenient for Kingston town centre and transport links
- Rent: £1,850 pcm

## Things to Do in Kingston upon Thames

Kingston upon Thames is one of south-west London’s most attractive and lively riverside destinations. It combines historic character, excellent shopping, beautiful open spaces and a wide choice of restaurants, cafés and leisure activities.

### Riverside Walks and Dining

The River Thames is one of Kingston’s greatest attractions. The riverside area offers scenic walking routes, waterside pubs, cafés and restaurants, making it ideal for a relaxed weekend stroll or evening meal. From Kingston, it is possible to walk along the river towards Hampton Wick, Teddington and Richmond, enjoying views of boats, bridges and surrounding greenery.

The riverside is also a popular setting for outdoor dining during the warmer months, with a range of independent venues and well-known restaurants overlooking the water.

### Shopping in Kingston Town Centre

Kingston is a major shopping destination in south-west London. The town centre includes the Bentall Centre, as well as a broad mixture of high-street retailers, independent shops, beauty services and specialist stores.

The historic Market Place is at the heart of Kingston and regularly hosts food stalls, seasonal markets and local events. It is a great place to browse for fresh produce, street food, gifts and handmade items.

### Historic Market Place and Ancient Market

Kingston has a long and fascinating history, and its market has existed for centuries. The Ancient Market Place remains one of the town’s most recognisable landmarks and provides a lively focal point for the area.

Nearby, visitors can see the famous Coronation Stone, traditionally associated with the crowning of several Saxon kings. This small but significant historic feature reflects Kingston’s important role in early English history.

### Theatre, Cinema and Entertainment

For entertainment, the Rose Theatre Kingston offers a varied programme of drama, comedy, music, talks and family productions throughout the year. It is a well-regarded cultural venue and a real asset to the local area.

Kingston also has a cinema in the town centre, making it easy to enjoy the latest film releases without travelling into central London. The area’s bars, pubs and restaurants provide plenty of options for an evening out.

### Parks and Green Spaces

Kingston is surrounded by excellent green space. Canbury Gardens, close to the river, is a popular location for picnics, walks and relaxation, while Fairfield Recreation Ground offers open parkland close to the town centre.

A short journey away is Richmond Park, one of London’s largest and most beautiful Royal Parks. Known for its roaming deer, wide-open landscapes, woodland and cycling routes, it is ideal for walking, running, photography and weekend outings.

Bushy Park, another nearby Royal Park, offers equally impressive open spaces, wildlife and long walking routes.

### Hampton Court Palace

Hampton Court Palace is easily accessible from Kingston and makes for an excellent day out. The former home of King Henry VIII is renowned for its spectacular Tudor architecture, historic state rooms, formal gardens and famous maze. The palace hosts exhibitions, family events, seasonal activities and outdoor concerts throughout the year.

### Water Activities on the Thames

For those who enjoy being on the water, Kingston offers opportunities for riverboat trips, paddleboarding, kayaking and rowing. Seasonal boat services can provide an enjoyable way to travel along the Thames towards Hampton Court, Richmond and other nearby riverside destinations.

### Food, Coffee and Local Dining

Kingston has a diverse food and drink scene, ranging from relaxed coffee shops and independent cafés to traditional pubs, international restaurants and riverside dining. Whether looking for brunch, a casual lunch, cocktails or a special evening meal, there are plenty of choices in and around the town centre.

### Excellent Access to London and Surrey

Kingston is well positioned for enjoying both London and Surrey. Regular rail services from Kingston station connect to Waterloo and other south-west London destinations, while local bus routes offer convenient access to Wimbledon, Richmond, New Malden, Surbiton and beyond.

This balance of riverside surroundings, urban convenience, green space and transport accessibility makes Kingston upon Thames a highly desirable place to live.
